papers.title: Sensitivity to Sterile Neutrinos with Elastic Neutrino-Electron and Highly Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering in the DUNE Near Detector
papers.abstract:
The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) is a next-generation neutrino experiment designed for precision measurements of long-baseline three-flavor neutrino oscillations. The DUNE Near Detector (ND) is also sensitive to short-baseline oscillations arising from mixing with an eV-scale sterile neutrino. In this paper, we present a sensitivity study for sterile-neutrino oscillations in the $3+1$ framework using three complementary event samples in the simulated DUNE ND: highly elastic $
u_\mu$ charged-current (CC), highly elastic $
u_e$ CC, and neutrino-electron elastic-scattering ($
u+e$) events. These highly exclusive samples are chosen to reduce neutrino-interaction and flux uncertainties: the low-hadronic-energy CC selections enhance the correlation between reconstructed lepton energy and neutrino energy, while the precisely calculable $
u+e$ cross section provides an independent constraint on the neutrino flux. Residual interaction-model dependence remains in the CC samples. The statistical analysis considers $|U_{e4}|^2$, $|U_{\mu4}|^2$, $|U_{	au4}|^2$, and $\Delta m^2$, with sensitivity results presented as fixed-$\Delta m^2$ slices for $|U_{	au4}|^2=0$. The strongest sensitivity occurs for $4 \lesssim \Delta m^2 \lesssim 10~\mathrm{eV}^2$, where oscillations produce resolvable distortions of the reconstructed-energy spectra. For one year of on-axis forward-horn-current running, the 90\% confidence-level sensitivity reaches approximately $|U_{\mu4}|^2 \simeq 0.01$ and $|U_{e4}|^2 \simeq 0.015$, depending on the value of the other mixing parameter.
papers.reason: Presents sensitivity studies for sterile neutrino oscillations using elastic neutrino-electron and neutrino-nucleus scattering samples in the DUNE Near Detector, squarely in the reader's core interests.

summary.tldr: DUNE Near Detector sensitivity to 3+1 sterile neutrinos is evaluated using low-hadronic-energy CC interactions and neutrino-electron elastic scattering flux constraints.
summary.novel_idea:
The paper combines highly elastic ($
u^{\mathrm{reco}} < 0.3	ext{ GeV}$) $
u_\mu$-CC and $
u_e$-CC interaction samples with $
u+e^-$ elastic scattering to perform a short-baseline sterile neutrino search exclusively within the DUNE Near Detector. Restricting the hadronic energy transfer suppresses nuclear and cross-section model dependencies and tightly couples the reconstructed lepton energy to the incident neutrino energy, while $
u+e^-$ scattering provides a precise electroweak constraint on the flux.
summary.method: Simulated forward horn current ($1.1\times 10^{21}$ POT) events in ND-LAr and the Temporary Muon Spectrometer (TMS) are analyzed across 102 reconstructed lepton energy bins. Systematic uncertainties spanning the DUNE flux model, 68 GENIE interaction parameters, detector response, and a 0.5% radiative correction error on $\nu-e$ scattering are formatted into a fixed fractional covariance matrix. A 4D parameter fit ($|U_{e4}|^2, |U_{\mu 4}|^2, |U_{\tau 4}|^2, \Delta m^2$) is executed with a Feldman-Cousins profile likelihood construction.
key_results: Peak 90% C.L. sensitivity reaches $|U_{\mu 4}|^2 \approx 0.01$ and $|U_{e4}|^2 \approx 0.015$ for $\Delta m^2 \sim 4-10 \text{ eV}^2$.

At $\Delta m^2 \lesssim 1 \text{ eV}^2$, sensitivity is limited by baseline length, whereas at $\Delta m^2 > 10 \text{ eV}^2$, spectral oscillations average out and sensitivity is driven by overall rate changes constrained by $\nu+e^-$ scattering.

The 90% C.L. Feldman-Cousins critical value is $\Delta\chi^2_{\mathrm{FC}} = 10.06$ (vs. Wilks expectation of 7.78 for 4 d.o.f.), with flux uncertainties causing the largest broadening of the test statistic distribution.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to DUNE Near Detector physics and oscillation systematics. It demonstrates how low-energy-transfer CC events, when paired with $\nu-e$ elastic scattering flux normalization, can isolate short-baseline BSM signatures while controlling nuclear model dependence.
summary.caveats: The analysis uses a fixed fractional covariance matrix evaluated at the null hypothesis and relies on GENIE 2.12.10 systematic variations; residual model dependence in the mapping between true and reconstructed low energy transfer could affect sample selection efficiency and bin migration.

papers.title: NuSTEC Review: Current Experimental and Theoretical Challenges of Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
papers.abstract: The precise measurement of neutrino properties is among the highest priorities in fundamental particle physics, involving many experimental and theoretical efforts worldwide. Since the experiments rely on the interactions of neutrinos in the nuclear environment, the planned advances in the scope and precision of these experiments require a commensurate effort in understanding and modeling the hadronic and nuclear physics of these interactions, as incorporated in neutrino event generators. This modeling is essential to every phase of the experimental analyses, and the theoretical uncertainties play an important role in interpreting experimental results. In this Review of current challenges, we summarize the open questions in neutrino-nucleus interactions at GeV-scale energies, and discuss in detail the potential impacts of these unknowns on the measurement of neutrino properties, using the determination of oscillation parameters as a central example. After an Executive Summary and a concise Overview of the issues, we address how the neutrino event generators treat these challenges, how electron-nucleus interactions can help understanding these challenges and the important unanswered questions for each underlying physics process---from quasi-elastic to deep-inelastic scattering. Across every topic, we find that current challenges can be met only through active support and collaboration among specialists in strong interactions and electroweak physics, including theorists and experimentalists from both the nuclear and high-energy physics communities.
papers.reason: A comprehensive review by NuSTEC covering current experimental and theoretical challenges in neutrino-nucleus scattering across all energy regimes and event generators, hitting the reader's core research profile perfectly. [favorite author: Isaacson]

summary.tldr: The NuSTEC collaboration reviews the current state, open challenges, and strategic priorities in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling for precision GeV-scale oscillation experiments.
summary.novel_idea: This comprehensive review acts as an updated global roadmap for the neutrino-scattering community following a decade of progress since the 2014 NuSTEC White Paper. It details the open theoretical and experimental issues across all kinematic regimes (QE, 2p2h/MEC, RES, SIS/DIS, FSI, CEvNS, coherent pion) and maps their direct impact on CP-violation and mass-ordering measurements at DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande, T2K, and NOvA.
summary.method: A synthesis of nuclear theory, experimental data, and event generator developments. The review evaluates theoretical models (ab initio, spectral functions, relativistic Fermi gas, GiBUU), generator implementations (GENIE, NuWro, NEUT, Achilles, GiBUU), electron-nucleus scattering constraints ($e,e'$ and $e,e'p$), hadron-nucleus transport data, and flux determination techniques.
key_results: Identifies 3-5% interaction systematic uncertainties in current oscillation analyses as the primary bottleneck to reaching the 1-2% statistical precision targets of DUNE and Hyper-K.

Establishes 6 critical priorities: funding theoretical nuclear models for relativistic dynamics and FSI; modular generator architectures and standard interfaces; detailed measurements of exclusive hadronic final states (neutrons, low-threshold protons, multi-pions); expanded electron/hadron scattering campaigns; standardized model-independent cross-section reporting; and dedicated hadron production experiments.
Highlights the lack of final-state neutron data and low-momentum hadron/pion transport constraints as major vulnerabilities for calorimetric and tracking detectors.
summary.why_it_matters: Must-read benchmark document for theoretical neutrino-nucleus physicists and generator developers. Co-authored by key experts in the field, it provides a comprehensive overview of the open problems in electroweak nuclear response, axial form factors, and FSI modeling.
summary.caveats: As a review and strategy document, it does not present new original calculations or fresh experimental data releases, but summarizes the current consensus and open issues across the field.

papers.title: Machine learning assisted $\nu/\bar{\nu}$ discrimination in atmospheric neutrino events for CPV sensitivity in a 20-kton liquid scintillator detector
papers.abstract: Atmospheric neutrinos span a broad range of energies and baselines, offering a complementary probe of leptonic CP violation. However, a JUNO-like liquid scintillator detector without a magnetic field cannot directly separate neutrino and antineutrino interactions, reducing CP violation sensitivity. This study investigates whether machine learning based statistical separation can improve CP violation sensitivity in a 20-kton detector. $\nu_{\mu}$ and $\nu_e$ charged current events are generated with GENIE (using Honda flux) in a JUNO-like detector geometry and are reweighted using OscProb three flavor oscillation probabilities incorporating Earth matter effects and NuFIT parameters. Detector response is approximated by smearing lepton and hadronic energies, neutrino direction, and neutron multiplicity. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers are trained on inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and charged lepton energy, with XGBoost selected for the analysis. CP violation sensitivity is evaluated for a 200 kton-year exposure using a Poisson likelihood with systematic nuisance parameters and marginalization over five oscillation parameters within their respective $3\sigma$ ranges. XGBoost achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of approximately 0.83 for both flavor samples. Under the square root approximation, peak CP violation sensitivity improves from 1.49 $\sigma$ to 1.96 $\sigma$ for normal mass ordering and from 1.14 $\sigma$ to 1.61 $\sigma$ for inverted mass ordering. Machine learning based statistical neutrino-antineutrino separation can recover part of the CP violation sensitivity lost in charge blind detectors. These preliminary results motivate further studies incorporating validated detector response and systematic uncertainties.
papers.reason: Investigates machine learning-assisted neutrino/antineutrino discrimination in atmospheric neutrinos for CP violation sensitivity in a liquid scintillator detector, matching core experimental/phenomenological oscillation interests.

summary.tldr: Machine learning trained on inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and lepton energy enables statistical $\nu/\bar{\nu}$ separation in unmagnetized liquid scintillator detectors, boosting atmospheric CPV sensitivity.
summary.novel_idea: Demonstrates that unmagnetized 20-kton liquid scintillator detectors (such as JUNO) can partially overcome lepton charge-blindness in atmospheric neutrino interactions by using machine learning classifiers on hadronic observables ($y$, $n_{\mathrm{fn}}$, $E_\ell$) to statistically separate $\nu$ and $\bar{\nu}$ events.
summary.method: Atmospheric $\nu_\mu$-CC and $\nu_e$-CC events are generated in GENIE (Honda flux) and reweighted with 3-flavor oscillation probabilities including Earth matter effects. Reconstructed lepton/hadronic energies, directions, and neutron multiplicities (90% tagging efficiency) are generated via parameterized smearing. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and MLP models are trained; XGBoost is selected to evaluate CPV sensitivity for a 200 kton-year exposure via a Poisson likelihood incorporating 7 systematic parameters and marginalization over 5 oscillation parameters.
key_results: XGBoost achieves an AUC of ~0.83 for both $\nu_\mu$ and $\nu_e$ CC event separation.
Neutron multiplicity is the single most dominant feature for classification (~77-79% relative importance).

Peak CPV sensitivity for a 200 kton-year exposure improves from $1.49\sigma$ (charge-blind) to $1.96\sigma$ (ML-assisted) under Normal Ordering, and from $1.14\sigma$ to $1.61\sigma$ under Inverted Ordering.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant for atmospheric neutrino phenomenology and ML applications in detector physics; underscores the physical importance of final-state neutron multiplicity in distinguishing neutrino vs antineutrino interactions in dense detector media.
summary.caveats: Uses fast parameterized Gaussian/binomial smearing rather than full detector optical simulation and particle reconstruction; assumes a fixed 90% neutron tagging efficiency; profiles oscillation parameters within $3\sigma$ while fixing the $\theta_{23}$ octant at best fit.

papers.title: Electroweak Parton Distribution Functions for Future Lepton Colliders
papers.abstract: At future high-energy colliders, such as a multi-TeV muon collider or the high-energy stages of an $e^+e^-$ linear collider, collinear radiation of electroweak gauge bosons becomes a dominant phenomenon. In this regime, many key processes are primarily initiated by photons and gauge bosons originating from lepton splittings. Electroweak Parton Distribution Functions (EW PDFs) provide an appropriate framework to describe these interactions by resumming large collinear logarithms arising from all possible Standard Model splittings, thereby enabling a partonic interpretation of the hard scattering. The formalism is particularly suitable for studying new physics beyond the Standard Model in the electroweak sector at higher scales. In this paper, we present the implementation of the EW PDF formalism within the Monte Carlo event generator \texttt{Whizard}. We demonstrate several applications of this framework and analyze its interplay with full fixed-order calculations as well as the purely kinematic Effective Weak Boson Approximation. We highlight scenarios where the EW PDF approach is especially useful for phenomenology and physics-potential studies for future lepton colliders. The EW PDF formalism is a vital step towards the ``electroweak jet regime'' where electroweak particles behave similarly to QCD jets.
papers.reason: Presents the implementation of Electroweak Parton Distribution Functions within Whizard for multi-TeV lepton colliders (muon colliders/linear colliders), squarely addressing the electroweak jet and high-energy neutrino/lepton collider physics regime. [favorite author: Tao Han]

summary.tldr: A fully resummed Electroweak Parton Distribution Function (EW PDF) framework is implemented in the Whizard event generator for multi-TeV lepton colliders.
summary.novel_idea: Integrates the complete SM Electroweak PDF (EW PDF) framework—which resums collinear electroweak gauge boson and fermion splittings across all helicity states—into the generic automated Monte Carlo generator Whizard, enabling partonic physics studies at high-energy lepton and muon colliders.
summary.method: Solves generalized DGLAP evolution equations in the unbroken $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ SM gauge theory including chiral couplings, gauge boson polarization states, and mass threshold matching. Numerical grids are integrated into Whizard. Detailed benchmark comparisons are performed for a 10 TeV $\mu^+\mu^-$ collider against full fixed-order diagrammatic calculations and the Effective Weak Boson Approximation (EWA) for $HH$, $t\bar{t}$, $\nu_\tau\bar{\nu}_\tau$, $WW$, and heavy scalar $XX$ production, alongside QED/QCD mini-jets below the EW scale.
key_results: Low-energy QCD mini-jet production ($gg \to jj$) via QED splittings is shown to be a massive background at a 10 TeV muon collider, with cross sections reaching $\mathcal{O}(10-100\text{ pb})$.

EW PDFs accurately match fixed-order matrix elements for longitudinal VBF processes ($HH, t\bar{t}$) at high invariant masses, exhibiting a 5-20% resummation suppression relative to leading-order EWA.

Demonstrates that the transverse mass scale $2H_T$ is significantly superior to $\sqrt{\hat{s}}/2$ for managing scale uncertainties and describing transverse kinematics in gauge-boson-initiated scattering.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to theoretical interest in electroweak resummation, QED/EW parton showers, and multi-TeV muon collider phenomenology. Provides a Monte Carlo tool to compute processes where electroweak gauge symmetry is manifest in initial-state splittings.
summary.caveats: The current framework does not yet link electroweak beam remnants to standard QCD hadronization/parton showers; collinear factorized approximations break down near kinematic endpoints ($x \to 1$) and forward low-$p_T$ gauge boson scattering where gauge cancellations dominate.

papers.title: Domain Adaptive Graph Neural Networks for Neutrino Experiments
papers.abstract: Weakly interacting particles such as neutrinos require highly efficient and precise detection methods to enable searches for new physics. Deep learning, and particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), has shown promise for reconstruction tasks in liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC) neutrino experiments. However, differences between simulations and experimental data introduce domain shifts that can degrade model performance and potentially mimic or obscure new-physics signals. Here, we demonstrate that robust learning across datasets can still be achieved by using domain adaptation during training. We introduce, to our knowledge for the first time, domain-adaptation-enabled GNNs for robust LArTPC reconstruction tasks. We use MicroBooNE open dataset as our labeled source domain, and introduce four perturbed datasets as our unlabeled target domains-- including a fixed scale variation, moderate and severe gaussian noise, and a signal variation as a function of the position in the detector. The inclusion of adversarial-based domain adaptation during training improves performance for all four target domains, without a substantial drop in performance in the source domain. Precision in the target domain was improved up to 0.19 and recall up to 0.37, depending on the variation and the network task. These results demonstrate a potential of domain adaptation to bridge the gap between simulations and experiments, and build more trustworthy models for current and future LArTPC neutrino experiments.
papers.reason: Applies adversarial-based domain adaptation to Graph Neural Networks for LArTPC neutrino experiments, directly tackling simulation-to-data shifts in MicroBooNE.

summary.tldr: Domain-adversarial training integrated into Graph Neural Networks (NuGraph3) mitigates performance degradation caused by simulation-to-data domain shifts in LArTPC event reconstruction.
summary.novel_idea: Applies Domain-Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for LArTPC hit filtering and semantic segmentation, enforcing domain-invariant latent space representations to prevent ML reconstruction model performance from degrading when moving from simulation to target experimental data.
summary.method: Evaluates the hierarchical GNN NuGraph3 using MicroBooNE open simulation data as the labeled source domain and 4 synthetic target domains representing common detector domain shifts: fixed scale variation, moderate Gaussian noise, severe Gaussian noise, and drift-time-dependent electron diffusion (RMS) shift. Adversarial training is enforced using a domain classifier and Gradient Reversal Layer (GRL) applied to the latent node embeddings.
key_results: Adversarial domain adaptation recovers target-domain precision losses by up to 0.19 and recall losses by up to 0.37 across perturbed target datasets.
In the severe Gaussian noise scenario, target semantic precision and recall rebound from 0.67 (without DA) to 0.86 (with DA).
Under fixed scaling, target filter recall is restored from 0.56 to 0.93 while maintaining source domain performance within 1% of the baseline model.
summary.why_it_matters: Addresses a key challenge in ML applications for LArTPC experiments (MicroBooNE, SBN, DUNE): the risk that subtle discrepancies between Monte Carlo simulations and detector data create domain shifts that degrade reconstruction efficiency or induce systematic bias.
summary.caveats: Evaluated on synthetic perturbations of the MicroBooNE open dataset rather than unblinded real experimental data; adversarial DA training introduces a ~5% computational time overhead per epoch.

papers.title: Flavor decomposition of the nucleon axial and tensor charges from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We determine the nucleon axial and tensor charges using four ensembles of twisted-mass clover-improved fermions with approximately equal physical volumes of about 5.5~fm and four lattice spacings, $ a=0.05$~fm, 0.06~fm, 0.07~fm, and 0.08~fm. The mass of the degenerate up and down, strange and charm quarks are tuned to approximately their physical values. We compute both connected and disconnected contributions to determine the isovector and isoscalar charges and their flavour decomposition. For the nucleon isovector axial charge we find $g_A^{u-d}=1.263(34)(26)$, in agreement with the experimental value. For the isoscalar axial charge we find $g_A^{u+d}=0.458(16)(1)$, while for the corresponding tensor charges we find $g_T^{u-d}=0.951(21)(5)$ and $g_T^{u+d}=0.556(16)(5)$.
papers.reason: Determines the nucleon isovector and isoscalar axial and tensor charges using twisted-mass lattice QCD with physical quark masses, directly core.

summary.tldr: The ETMC determines the nucleon axial and tensor charges, including flavor decomposition, using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass clover-improved ensembles directly at the physical pion mass.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike prior lattice calculations that rely on chiral extrapolations from heavier-than-physical pion masses, this work performs simulations directly at physical quark masses across four lattice spacings ($a=0.05$ to $0.08$ fm, with constant physical volumes $\sim 5.5$ fm), thus avoiding uncontrolled chiral extrapolation systematics.
summary.method: Evaluates connected and disconnected contributions using twisted-mass clover-improved fermions. Computes RI'-MOM renormalization factors and converts to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at $\mu = 2$ GeV. Applies a two-step fitting strategy and performs $a^2$ continuum extrapolations model-averaged via the Akaike information criterion.
key_results: Isovector axial charge: $g_A^{u-d} = 1.263(34)(26)$, consistent with experiment.
Isoscalar axial charge: $g_A^{u+d} = 0.458(16)(1)$.
Isovector tensor charge: $g_T^{u-d} = 0.951(21)(5)$.
Isoscalar tensor charge: $g_T^{u+d} = 0.556(16)(5)$.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides first-principles lattice inputs for nucleon axial and tensor form factors and charges, which are vital for constraining BSM interactions in neutrino scattering (DUNE, COHERENT) and interpreting neutron beta decay and neutrinoless double-beta decay.
summary.caveats: Connected contributions rely on two-state fits and summation methods to control excited-state contamination, and disconnected loops require advanced noise-reduction techniques (deflation, one-end trick, hierarchical probing).

papers.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
papers.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.
papers.reason: Analyzes fixed points, period doubling, and chaos in collisional neutrino flavor conversion for supernovae and neutron star mergers, squarely in core neutrino astrophysics.

summary.tldr: Homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations are constructed for two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisions, revealing persistent oscillations, period-doubling bifurcations, and chaos.
summary.novel_idea: Extends collision-balanced stationary solutions to arbitrary discrete or continuous energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates, and demonstrates that these stationary populations accurately estimate time-averaged flavor populations even inside chaotic regimes.
summary.method: Formulates self-consistency equations for isotropic collective-precession states in quantum kinetic equations incorporating flavor self-interactions and collisional relaxation. Analyzes linear stability via Jacobian eigenvalues and tracks periodic orbits up to 256-cycles to study transitions to chaos.
key_results: Identifies a period-doubling route to chaos in neutrino flavor conversion with spacing ratios approaching the Feigenbaum constant $\delta_{\text{F}} \simeq 4.669$.
The leading Lyapunov exponent for the chaotic trajectory is $\widehat{\lambda}_1 \simeq 2.8 \times 10^{-3}$.
Stationary population fixed points predict time-averaged flavor occupations to within $10\%$ across periodic and chaotic regimes without parameter tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts supernova and neutron star merger neutrino transport modeling by providing physically motivated population fixed points for collisional flavor instability (CFI) subgrid schemes.
summary.caveats: Assumes an isotropic background to isolate the collision-flavor balance, though selected 1D spatial box tests indicate the HCP estimates remain robust despite spatial inhomogeneities.

papers.title: Unpolarized proton PDF with physical quark masses and large momenta
papers.abstract: We present a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculation of the proton isovector ($u-d$) unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) at physical sea and valence quark masses, using Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears within the large-momentum effective theory framework. The calculation is performed on a (2+1)-flavor ensemble with a lattice spacing of $a=0.076$ fm and proton momenta up to $2.3$ GeV. We combine kinematically enhanced nucleon interpolating operators, the Coulomb-gauge method, and high-statistics measurements to improve the signal quality at large momenta and quark separations. We use the static regularization-independent momentum subtraction and hybrid schemes to renormalize the bare matrix elements. The light-cone PDF in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme is obtained from the quasi-PDF through next-to-leading-order (NLO) perturbative matching supplemented by next-to-leading-logarithmic renormalization-group resummation. With reduced uncertainties, the resulting PDF is consistent with our previous calculation on a similar lattice ensemble with $a=0.06$~fm and a valence pion mass of 300 MeV. Notably, despite the reduced uncertainties, the agreement with the phenomenological PDF persists over the longitudinal momentum fraction range $0.25\lesssim|x|\lesssim0.75$, where the lattice calculation is expected to be reliable. This agreement is further supported by a comparison in coordinate space, where our short-distance lattice matrix elements are consistent with those obtained from the phenomenological PDF through NLO matching. In particular, we observe close agreement in the imaginary part for the first time. Together, these results represent an encouraging step toward precision benchmarking of lattice QCD calculations of PDFs.
papers.topic: Unpolarized proton PDF from lattice QCD
papers.reason: Lattice QCD calculation of the proton isovector unpolarized PDF at physical quark masses using large-momentum effective theory, directly aligned with nucleon structure interests.

summary.tldr: A high-statistics lattice QCD calculation of the proton isovector unpolarized PDF at physical quark masses using Coulomb-gauge quark bilinears within LaMET shows good agreement with phenomenology.
summary.novel_idea: Combines Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears (avoiding linear Wilson-line divergences and renormalons) with kinematically enhanced interpolating operators and hybrid/SRI'-MOM renormalization at physical quark masses to benchmark light-cone PDFs.
summary.method: Calculated on a $64^3 \times 64$ HISQ $(2+1)$-flavor ensemble at $a = 0.076$ fm with proton momenta $P_z = 1.8$ and $2.3$ GeV. Bare matrix elements are renormalized via SRI'-MOM (converted to $\overline{\text{MS}}$) and hybrid schemes, Fourier-transformed using NLA asymptotic tails, and matched at NLO with NLL renormalization-group resummation.
key_results: Renormalized coordinate-space matrix elements show close agreement with NNPDF4.0-based NLO reconstructions, notably observing close agreement in the imaginary part for the first time.
The resulting $\overline{\text{MS}}$ light-cone PDFs agree with global phenomenological fits in the moderate-to-large longitudinal momentum fraction range $0.25 \lesssim |x| \lesssim 0.75$.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a rigorous first-principles lattice benchmark for the unpolarized isovector PDF ($u-d$) using modern LaMET and Coulomb-gauge techniques, strengthening theoretical control for DUNE, JLab, and EIC cross-section analyses.
summary.caveats: Calculations are performed at a single lattice spacing, precluding a direct continuum limit, and rely on NLO matching and NLA asymptotic extrapolations to stabilize the Fourier transform.

papers.title: Collective Signatures of Pionic Correlations at High Momentum Transfer
papers.abstract: High-momentum-transfer reactions have provided experimental evidence for enhanced pionic correlations in nuclei, yet the microscopic connection between the low-energy pionic response and the delta-hole excitation spectrum remains unresolved. Here we identify hybrid pion-delta collective modes that emerge through the coherent coupling of nucleon-hole and delta-hole excitations. By evaluating the full delta-hole Lindhard function within the random-phase approximation, we find a robust low-energy hybrid pion-delta mode and a higher-energy collective delta-hole mode. The low-energy mode is strongly enhanced as the Landau-Migdal parameter is reduced, exhibiting behavior characteristic of a precursor to pion condensation. We further show that these modes may be probed through high-momentum-transfer charged-pion production reactions. Because the same collective pion-delta function governs both the response and the RPA correlation energy, our results connect experimentally observable collective excitations with microscopic many-body correlations.
papers.reason: Identifies hybrid pion-delta collective modes via RPA evaluation of the delta-hole Lindhard function, directly addressing low-energy pionic responses and nuclear electroweak interactions.

summary.tldr: Evaluation of the full delta-hole Lindhard function within the RPA reveals low-energy hybrid pion-delta collective modes that act as precursors to pion condensation and link to nuclear binding.
summary.novel_idea: Performs explicit full Fermi-sea integration of the $\Delta$-hole Lindhard function on equal footing with nucleon-hole excitations, rather than using single-energy approximations, demonstrating a substantial low-energy $\Delta h$ tail that drives collective modes.
summary.method: Evaluates $Nh$ and $\Delta h$ susceptibilities and sums ring diagrams to all orders within the random-phase approximation (RPA) using a pion-exchange plus Landau-Migdal ($g'$) spin-isospin effective interaction.
key_results: Identifies a robust low-energy hybrid pion-delta mode around $\omega \sim 0.2 m_\pi$ at momentum transfers $q \sim 3 m_\pi$ that is strongly enhanced as $g'$ decreases.
Including $\Delta h$ excitations increases the magnitude of the RPA correlation energy by nearly a factor of four (e.g., from $-13.1$ MeV to $-56.6$ MeV at $g' = 0.45$).
Demonstrates that the collective pion-delta function governs both the dynamical response and the RPA correlation energy.
summary.why_it_matters: Connects microscopic many-body correlations and nuclear binding energy to high-momentum-transfer neutrino and hadron-induced reactions sensitive to the longitudinal spin-isospin response.
summary.caveats: Assumes a universal Landau-Migdal parameter and neglects isospin-symmetry breaking details, treating like-nucleon pair suppression phenomenologically via an effective $g'$ shift.

papers.title: A possible signature of neutrino spin precession in the J-PARC muon $g-2$ experiment
papers.abstract: We examine a possible signature of the neutrino angular-momentum contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly measurement in the J-PARC E34 experiment. In previous papers we argued that the angular momentum carried by the unobserved neutrino pair may leave an uncertainty in the anomaly inferred from the time modulation of detected positrons. At Fermilab the highly relativistic muons make the forward-emission approximation suitable for this estimate. The lower muon momentum at J-PARC requires the decay kinematics to be treated explicitly. We integrate the longitudinal momentum of the neutrino pair using the positron energy distribution and asymmetry derived from the theoretical weak-decay spectrum, and the same event-counting weight $N(E)A(E)$ is employed for both experiments. For positron energies between $1.5$ and $2.9$ GeV at Fermilab and between $200$ and $275$ MeV at J-PARC, the proposed correction is smaller at J-PARC by $0.415\pm0.176$ ppm, when the most optimistic E34 precision is assumed. The expected difference amounts to $2.36$ standard deviations if the future measurement is centred on this value. The calculation thus identifies an experimental comparison which may test the proposed effect independently of the hadronic contribution to the Standard Model prediction. We also examine the possibility of testing the effect by comparing measurements at two different muon momenta. With a fixed positron energy threshold of 200 MeV, the maximum sensitivity is obtained at a muon beam energy of 245 MeV. The predicted difference relative to the nominal J-PARC configuration has significance of $4.88\sigma$ for the most optimistic experimental sensitivity.
papers.topic: Neutrino spin precession in muon g-2
papers.reason: Examines the signature of neutrino angular momentum contribution and spin precession in the J-PARC E34 muon g-2 experiment from unobserved neutrino pairs in decay kinematics, directly connecting neutrino physics to precision muon anomalies.

summary.tldr: Calculates the kinematic signature of neutrino angular momentum precession in the J-PARC E34 muon $g-2$ experiment and proposes a two-momentum comparison to test it with $5\sigma$ sensitivity.
summary.novel_idea: Accounts explicitly for non-collinear decay kinematics of lower-momentum muons at J-PARC—unlike the forward-emission approximation used at Fermilab—to test whether unobserved neutrino angular momentum shifts the inferred magnetic anomaly.
summary.method: Integrates the longitudinal momentum of the neutrino pair using the theoretical weak-decay spectrum, positron energy distributions, and asymmetries with the same $N(E)A(E)$ counting weights for both Fermilab and J-PARC configurations.
key_results: The proposed neutrino angular-momentum correction is smaller at J-PARC than at Fermilab by $0.415 \pm 0.176$ ppm in the optimistic E34 scenario ($2.36\sigma$ separation).

A proposed two-momentum test at J-PARC (comparing $300$ MeV/$c$ with an optimal beam momentum of $221.4$ MeV/$c$) reaches a maximum significance of $4.88\sigma$ under optimistic experimental assumptions.
summary.why_it_matters: Offers a method to test anomalous contributions to muon $g-2$ measurements independently of theoretical hadronic vacuum polarization uncertainties.
summary.caveats: The forecast assumes ideal theoretical decay spectra and does not incorporate detailed detector acceptance, beam optics, or experimental extraction weights for either laboratory.

papers.title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
papers.abstract: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.
papers.topic: Isospin violation in neutron weak magnetism
papers.reason: Examines isospin-violating effects from quark mass differences and electromagnetism on the neutron weak magnetic moment in beta decay using constituent quark models, directly addressing precision CVC and nucleon electroweak form factors.

papers.title: Pion and kaon electromagnetic form factors in a flavor-dressed contact interaction: the role of Nf-screening on dynamical chiral symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: We compute the electromagnetic form factors of the pion and the kaon in a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose effective coupling depends on the number of active light flavors Nf , so that dynamical chiral symmetry breaking is screened as Nf grows toward the chiral transition. The calculation uses the rainbow-ladder truncation of the Schwinger-Dyson and Bethe-Salpeter equations with proper-time regularization, and it includes the dressed quark-photon vertex obtained from its own inhomogeneous Bethe-Salpeter equation in the same truncation. At Nf = 2 the model reproduces the established contact interaction values of the meson masses, decay constants and condensates, and the charge radii rpi = 0.447 fm and rK = 0.417 fm, which undershoot experiment by about one third, as is known for this class of interactions. We therefore restrict every comparison to Q2 less then or equal to 0.6 GeV2, confront it with the NA7 data and with one-loop chiral perturbation theory, and focus on the response to Nf . Both radii grow monotonically with Nf , and the growth survives every variation of the screening function and of the infrared confinement scale that we test. The growth is carried by the quark core rather than by the vector-meson dressing: between Nf = 2 and 6 the bare-vertex contribution to <r2pi> rises from 0.097 to 0.226 fm2, while the dressing contribution moves from 0.102 to 0.127 fm2 even though the rho pole drops from 0.93 to 0.70 GeV. The finite strange mass slows the kaon response only moderately.
papers.reason: Computes electromagnetic form factors of pions and kaons using Schwinger-Dyson equations with dynamical chiral symmetry breaking, highly relevant to hadron structure inputs for neutrino physics.

papers.title: Real Intermediate States in Dark Matter Freeze-In from First Principles: Single Mediator
papers.abstract: We investigate the treatment of real intermediate states (RIS) in freeze-in production of $s$-channel Dark Matter (DM) with unstable mediators, as such models feature a double-counting issue when decay and annihilation collision terms are simply added within the semi-classical Boltzmann approach and a finite width is used for the regularization of the resonance. While several ad-hoc RIS-subtraction schemes are available to mitigate this problem, a first-principles treatment in this context is so far missing. We therefore start from the Closed-Time-Path (CTP) formulation of non-equilibrium Quantum Field Theory and present a CTP-based description of $s$-channel freeze-in pair production of a single scalar, fermion or vector DM species. In addition to being intrinsically free of non-unitary overcounting, the CTP ansatz also has the advantage of systematically capturing thermal corrections known to be important for DM freeze-in. Separate evolution equations assuming a single scalar or vector mediator in thermal equilibrium with the surrounding bath are presented. The exact propagators of the unstable mediators are approximated by resumming one particle irreducible (1PI) self-energy diagrams generated by bath particles and are evaluated with their full mass and momentum dependence in contrast to the commonly adopted Hard Thermal Loop limit. The CTP relic densities are compared numerically with those obtained using the most common RIS-subtraction schemes for two example $s$-channel freeze-in models, demonstrating the phenomenological relevance of a consistent RIS treatment.
papers.reason: Examines real intermediate states in dark matter freeze-in using Closed-Time-Path non-equilibrium QFT, directly overlapping with thermal field theory methods used for low-energy and dark sector portals.

papers.title: Evidence for quark+quark pairing in proton formation
papers.abstract: The question of pairing between quarks inside baryons is addressed by calculating the fragmentation functions that describe production of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in high-energy collisions and comparing attendant predictions with phenomenological global fits to available data and directly with data on hadron multiplicities. The fragmentation functions are obtained from nucleon parton distribution functions using the Drell-Levy-Yan relation and subsequently solving a coupled set of pion, kaon, and nucleon jet cascade equations. Strong empirical evidence is found for the presence of diquark correlations. In comparison with global fits, $d$ (down) quark to proton fragmentation ($d\to p$) exhibits the clearest signals. The strongest evidence is found in comparisons with the momentum-dependent proton multiplicity distribution: FFs built from a proton wave function that contains diquark correlations deliver a $z$-profile that is fully consistent with available data, whereas that obtained from a no-pairing wave function is disfavoured by data at the $9\sigma$ level.
papers.reason: Calculates nucleon fragmentation functions and finds empirical evidence for diquark correlations in proton formation, directly aligning with nucleon structure and scattering final states.

papers.title: Quantum Open Effective Field Theory: anomalous decoherence
papers.abstract: We study decoherence of a scalar field coupled to ``anomalous'' environments with critical behavior with the Schwinger-Keldysh including the influence functional, and the quantum master equation (QME) up to second order in the coupling. The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation yields a Langevin equation and the Lindblad (QME) includes \emph{time dependent rates} allowing to study transient dynamics. We focus on three examples featuring non-Markov dynamics that cannot be described with S-matrix/Fermi's golden rule rates \textbf{i) Unparticle physics:} a conformal sector beyond the Standard Model at an infrared fixed point featuring correlation functions with anomalous scaling dimensions, \textbf{ii) Threshold and infrared enhancement:} when the mass shell of the field coincides with or is near to a kinematic threshold of the spectral density of the bath, \textbf{iii) Critical environments:} the bath is at a critical point, correlation functions scale with anomalous dimensions and long-wavelength fluctuations feature critical slowing down. In all cases the reduced density matrix undergoes decoherence in the energy basis of the probe, and off-diagonal matrix elements decay as $e^{-\Phi(t)}$ with $\Phi(t)>0 $ the \emph{decoherence function} and $\Gamma(t) = \dot{\Phi}(t)$ the decoherence rate. In all cases we find that either transient or asymptotically $\Phi(t) \propto t^{-\mu}~;~ \mu>0$ with $\mu$, determined by the behavior of the spectral density at threshold and the anomalous scaling dimensions of the correlation functions, or $\Phi(t) \propto \ln(t)$ for the infrared case. For a critical environment there is a new dynamical scaling exponent. A probe of frequency $\omega_q$ is resonant with a \emph{critically slow} quasiparticle for $q_*\propto \omega^{1/z}_q$ at which decoherence is strongly \emph{enhanced}.
papers.reason: Studies decoherence and master equations for probes coupled to anomalous or critical environments (unparticle physics, thresholds), closely touching effective field theory and open quantum systems.

papers.title: Direct Light-Cone Reconstruction of the $B$-Meson Shape Function in HQET
papers.abstract: The $B$-meson shape function encodes the nonperturbative residual-momentum dynamics of the heavy quark within heavy quark effective theory (HQET). From a Wilsonian perspective, HQET provides a natural framework for lattice calculations when the heavy quark mass is comparable to or exceeds the inverse lattice spacing. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a $B$-meson quasi-shape function directly in HQET and calculate its one-loop matching to the light-cone shape function, avoiding an intermediate matching step involving a full-QCD light-cone distribution. We determine the one-loop renormalization kernels and matching coefficients in both the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ and regularization-independent momentum-subtraction (RI/MOM) schemes for the quasi-shape function, while keeping the light-cone shape function in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme. The matching coefficients are obtained at leading power in the large-$v^z$ expansion and are independent of the infrared regulator. Our results provide the perturbative ingredients for a direct lattice HQET determination of the $B$-meson shape function.
papers.reason: Introduces a B-meson quasi-shape function directly in HQET with one-loop matching for lattice QCD, highly relevant to heavy quark effective theory and precision B-physics.

papers.title: Short-range dynamics of $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ in a coupled-channel framework
papers.abstract: We study the short-range dynamics in the coupled-channel description of the $S$-wave $D \bar{D}^*$ and $DD^*$ systems for $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$, respectively. Contact interactions are related through scalar- and vector-meson exchange saturation, while pion exchange is included explicitly with its local term subtracted. The coupled Lippmann-Schwinger equations incorporate the self-energy of the unstable $D^*$ mesons, thereby accounting for the three-body $D \bar{D} \pi$ ($D D\pi$) dynamics. Fixing the contact interaction from the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ pole, we trace the predicted $X(3872)$ pole as the local magnetic dipole term from vector-meson exchange is varied. Retaining this term in full produces the shallowest poles, which remain approximately $5$--$12~\mathrm{MeV}$ below the observed $X(3872)$ mass. It is found that the pion exchange has a moderate effect on the binding energy and a stronger effect on the isospin violation for the $X(3872)$ state. The residual tension between the pure-molecular bound descriptions of $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ is analyzed with the Feshbach projection. This analysis indicates a $DD^*$ interaction weaker than that implied by the purely molecular fits, and shows that the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ state instead arises from the mixing of the $DD^{*}$ channel with a compact $cc\bar{u}\bar{d}$ state. We further examine the spatial structure using Born--Oppenheimer effective field theory. For separation radii of $0.5$--$1.5~\mathrm{fm}$, the combined charmonium and short-distance tetraquark weight in $X(3872)$ is $3.0$--$9.7\%$, while the short-distance weight in $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ is $1.3$--$14.4\%$. These results favor retaining the local vector-exchange contribution within the saturation framework and motivate a joint treatment of molecular and compact dynamics for the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$.
papers.reason: Studies short-range dynamics of X(3872) and T_cc(3875)+ in a coupled-channel framework with contact interactions and meson exchanges, closely aligned with hadronic molecular dynamics and EFT.

papers.title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
papers.abstract: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 \phi)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer R\'enyi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. We trace this behavior to a spin-density matrix of rank at most two with maximally mixed marginals. For this class of states, entanglement and Bell nonlocality coincide even when the state is mixed, while the explicit form of the light-front helicity amplitudes ensures that both persist in the whole phase space. We suggest accessing the spin correlations in unpolarized hadron collisions through the Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions. We point out that, in inclusive production, for massless quarks, suitably chosen double-Collins asymmetries provide promising entanglement witnesses.
papers.reason: Investigates spin-spin correlations, quantum entanglement, and Bell nonlocality of quark-antiquark pairs in hadronic collisions using TMDs and fragmentation functions, directly connecting to quantum information aspects of scattering.

papers.title: Symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory
papers.abstract: A symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of the non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory is introduced. Integral equations for the two-nucleon scattering and the deuteron structure functions are derived and numerical solutions at leading order are obtained.
papers.reason: Presents a symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of non-relativistic baryon chiral EFT with two-nucleon scattering solutions, directly relevant to nuclear and chiral EFT for electroweak processes.

papers.title: Origin of Tensor Polarized Structure of the Deuteron
papers.abstract: The microscopic origin of the deuteron tensor polarized structure function $b_1$ remains unresolved. Conventional nuclear models attribute a nonzero $b_1$ mainly to the $D$-wave component of the deuteron wave function, but generally fail to reproduce the magnitude and momentum-dependence observed by the HERMES experiment. Using a QCD-based light-front framework with degrees of freedom beyond the conventional nucleonic picture, in particular including hidden-color components and relativistic spin--momentum correlations, we find that a small but nonzero estimated hidden-color admixture can be sufficient to generate a substantial tensor response ($b_1(x)$), while it is essentially insensitive to the $D$-wave component. The physical $D$-wave probability of $0.85\%$, fixed by the empirical quadrupole moment, changes $b_1$ by only $1.7\%$, with the dominant contribution arising from the colored-cluster $S$-wave sector. These results demonstrate that the tensor-polarized structure of the deuteron is driven primarily by hidden-color dynamics rather than by the $D$-wave component.
papers.reason: Investigates the microscopic origin of the deuteron tensor polarized structure function b1 via a light-front framework including hidden-color components, highly relevant to nuclear structure and electron-scattering constraints.

papers.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
papers.abstract: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.
papers.reason: Demonstrates that reabsorption of Urca neutrinos strongly suppresses bulk-viscous damping in neutron star merger oscillations using an energy-resolved kinetic treatment, directly tying neutrino transport and interactions to neutron star dynamics.

papers.title: Nucleon transversity from dihadron data and x-dependent lattice QCD constraint
papers.abstract: We extract collinear transversity distributions and dihadron fragmentation functions in a joint neural-network analysis of dihadron production in electron-positron annihilation, semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering, and polarized proton-proton collisions. We incorporate lattice QCD calculation of isovector transversity, which constrains the up-down flavor differences for quarks and antiquarks over broad momentum fraction range complementary to data. Matched fits with and without the lattice input describe the experimental data comparably well. Including the lattice input shifts the down-valence distribution toward more negative values and enhances up-valence transversity at large $x$. The magnitude of the central down-valence result exceeds the reference Soffer inequalities, motivating further test of positivity constraints.
papers.reason: Extracts collinear transversity distributions and dihadron fragmentation functions via a joint neural-network analysis incorporating lattice QCD isovector transversity constraints, directly tied to nucleon structure and lattice inputs.

papers.title: M-theory anomaly localization and holographic $c$-extremization
papers.abstract: We compute the cubic and $C_3\wedge X_8$ caracteristic class contributions to the trial anomaly polynomial of supersymmetric $AdS_3\times M_8$ backgrounds with $M_8=P(\mathcal O \oplus \mathcal L)\to B_6$. Including the Abelian currents descending from $C_3$, we identify the projective invariant $J$ as the denominator arising from their elimination by $c$-extremization and recover the central charge $c^{(0)}=-I_3+3I_+I_-/J$. The $X_8$ push-forward determines the pure R-symmetry, mixed R--Betti and gravitational anomalies. Evaluating it at the classical extremum gives the associated central-charge corrections, linear in the overall unshifted flux. The mixed term contributes equally to both central charges and is required in general. We evaluate these formulae for three flux-quantized backgrounds, including non-polynomial solutions. Direct projective fibre integration reproduces the mixed coefficient obtained by localization. On the wrapped-$M5$ $S^4$ bundle, the same couplings reproduce the independently known field-theory anomaly through orders $N^3$ and $N$. Their interpretation as full CFT central charges requires a unitary SCFT with a normalizable vacuum, suitable supersymmetric boundary conditions, a complete mixing sector of global currents and control of omitted anomaly sectors. A conditional Euclidean relative-equivariant interpretation is discussed separately.
papers.reason: Computes characteristic class contributions to trial anomaly polynomials of supersymmetric AdS3 x M8 backgrounds and central charges via c-extremization, offering advanced field-theoretic and holographic tools relevant to precision SCFTs.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
papers.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $9.6\times10^{-42}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $\alpha\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.
papers.reason: Evaluates sub-GeV dark matter via the Migdal effect in LZ, directly relevant to low-energy atomic and nuclear probes of new physics.

papers.title: Constrained field-space estimators for background-field lattice QCD observables
papers.abstract: Background-field lattice calculations extract weak-field response coefficients from correlators computed at several field strengths. We treat this extraction as linear estimation in field space and compare fixed cancellation stencils with covariance-optimized, generalized-least-squares estimators of the same coefficient, using archival nucleon double ratios on about 1000 quenched configurations at six quark masses and decuplet correlators for which exact answers follow from the lattice contractions. The fixed $O(B^4)$-$O(B^8)$ stencils are nearly coincident and cost almost nothing in precision. Weight-free null-space tests reject the two-term response model in most nucleon ensembles; whether they reject the three-term model depends on the temporal fits and on the noise of the estimated temporal covariance, which raises the null-contrast error by a factor of 1.7-2.4. With that noise included, covariance optimization gains 1-2% in precision at the five lighter masses (3-30% with two-state time fits, which also lower moments by 3-10%) and nothing on independent data halves, while its weights carry three to four orders of magnitude more leverage on omitted response modes than the fixed stencils and move the moments by up to 1.8 marginal standard errors. The decuplet controls show what such leverage does under misspecification: the first-order responses obey $\mu_{\Delta^+}/\mu_{\Delta^{++}}=1/2$ and $\mu_{\Delta^0}=0$ exactly. The lowest-order estimate misses the first by 10-25 standard errors. The fixed $O(B^4)$-$O(B^8)$ stencils satisfy it within errors in the production windows, whereas the correlated linear fit in $B^2$, with the same constraints as the $O(B^4)$ stencil, misses it by 3-17%; the null-space test rejects that fit's model. The results distinguish statistical precision from robustness to omitted response modes; they are not physical-point magnetic moments.
papers.reason: Compares covariance-optimized and fixed stencils for background-field lattice QCD response coefficients using nucleon and decuplet correlators.

papers.title: Renormalized symmetry probes for emergent symmetries and non-chiral lattice fermions
papers.abstract: The degeneracy of hadron correlators in symmetry-related channels signals symmetry restoration in high-temperature QCD. RG-invariant probes of this degeneracy need care when the regularization breaks chiral symmetry, or when the symmetry is not exact in the massless action, as for the emergent chiral-spin symmetry $SU(2)_{CS}$. We renormalize the thermal and screening meson correlators of every flavor sector by the thermal correlator of the same channel in the $\bar ud$ sector at a common reference point. The symmetry ratio $\kappa_{AB}$ then depends on the renormalization only through the ratio $R_{AB}$. For exact symmetries, $R_{AB}=1$ and $\kappa_{AB}$ is RG invariant and scheme independent in mass-independent schemes. For emergent symmetries, $R_{AB}\neq1$ carries the relative logarithmic cutoff dependence of the two channels, which cancels in $\kappa_{AB}$, and the residual dependence on the reference scale is physical. The framework applies to Wilson, twisted-mass and staggered fermions, where $R_{AB}$ absorbs the channel-dependent renormalization, and the tensor pair $(T_k,X_k)$ keeps $R_{T_kX_k}=1$ on isotropic Wilson-type lattices. Lattice artifacts are a small correction to the chiral-spin probes $\kappa_{CS}$ and $\kappa_{fade}$, but as large as the signal of the exact-symmetry probes. For free quarks, we derive $\kappa_{fade}=2/3$ for every mass and separation, and $\kappa_{CS}\le1/3$. We apply the renormalized probes to $N_f=2+1+1$ QCD with optimal domain-wall quarks at the physical point, with $a=0.064$ fm and $T=192$-$1539$ MeV. The hierarchical restoration of the chiral symmetries from the light to the charm sectors is confirmed, and is invariant under renormalization. The $\bar uc$ and $\bar sc$ sectors have the widest chiral-spin windows, also at a tighter threshold. Thus spin-1 mesons with one charm quark are the most attractive channels for the chiral-spin regime.
papers.topic: Renormalized symmetry probes in lattice QCD
papers.reason: Develops RG-invariant symmetry ratios for thermal and screening meson correlators across various fermion discretizations, highly relevant to lattice studies of chiral and emergent symmetries.

papers.title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
papers.abstract: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.
papers.reason: Computes the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-N_c limit using Twisted Eguchi-Kawai reduced models and lattice fermions, relevant to non-perturbative QCD structure.

papers.title: Observation of a strange $J^P=1^{-}$ resonance $K^{*}_1(1870)$ in $\chi_{c1}\to K^+K^-\eta^{\prime}$ decays
papers.abstract: A partial wave analysis of the process $\psi(2S)\to \gamma\chi_{c1}$, $\chi_{c1}\to K^{+}K^{-}\eta^{\prime}$, with the $\eta^{\prime}$ meson reconstructed in the $\pi^+\pi^-\gamma$ and $\pi^+\pi^-\eta$ decay modes, is performed using a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3)\times10^{6}$ $\psi(2S)$ events collected with the BESIII detector. In the $K\eta^{\prime}$ system, a resonant contribution with quantum numbers $J^{P}=1^{-}$ is observed for the first time and is denoted as the $K_1^*(1870)$ meson. Its statistical significance is $11.0\sigma$, and its mass and width are measured to be $M=(1869.0 \pm 14.6\pm 18.6$) MeV/$c^{2}$ and $\Gamma=(167.3 \pm 34.0\pm 24.2$) MeV, respectively. The branching fraction of the $\chi_{c1}\to K^{\mp}K_1^*(1870)^{\pm}\to K^{+}K^{-}\eta^{\prime}$ decay chain is determined to be $(1.48 \pm 0.30\pm 0.33)\times10^{-5}$. The branching fraction of the $\chi_{c1}\to K^{+}K^{-}\eta^{\prime}$ decay is measured to be $(7.90 \pm 0.48)\times10^{-4}$. Several intermediate scalar, vector, and tensor states are required to provide a good description of the data. These results provide new input for understanding strange-meson spectroscopy and investigating possible hybrid-state candidates.
papers.reason: BESIII partial wave analysis observing a strange J^P=1- resonance in chi_c1 decays, providing new input for strange-meson spectroscopy. [favorite author: Tao Han]

papers.title: $B\to$ invisible decays as probes of light new physics
papers.abstract: Rare $B$ decays with missing energy probe heavy particles contributing to $b\to s\nu\bar\nu$ and new light states produced on shell. We discuss both possibilities in light of the Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+\Emiss$. Fits to the missing-mass distribution favour a two-body contribution near $2.1\,\GeV$, while scalar and fermion pairs of masses around $0.4$-$0.6\,\GeV$ remain viable alternatives. Extracting their couplings would profit from additional measurements, including the $B\to K^*\Emiss$ rate and longitudinal $K^*$ polarization, together with invisible $B_s$ decays which constrain scalar-pair interactions. We discuss how an aligned Higgsed $U(1)'$ model can realize the single-vector explanation through a vector-like top partner. Loop-induced electroweak mixing makes visible $Z'$ decays unavoidable, requiring an additional invisible channel to evade dimuon searches. We show that a light dark fermion can provide this channel and also account for the observed dark matter abundance through resonant thermal annihilation.
papers.topic: Rare B Decays and Missing Energy
papers.reason: Analyzes rare B decays with missing energy and light dark sector explanations for experimental excesses, relevant to BSM searches tied to neutrino and meson facilities.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of semileptonic $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ and $B_c\to(\eta_c,B,B_s)$ decays in the light-front quark model
papers.abstract: We present a global analysis of the semileptonic transitions $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ and $B_c\to(\eta_c,B,B_s)$ by comparing five potential-model implementations of the QCD-motivated light-front quark model. We use the same fully Bakamjian--Thomas-based prescription for the weak current in all five models and keep their respective spectroscopic parameters fixed. We examine how confinement, radial mixing, and the treatment of hyperfine interactions jointly affect the form factors, differential decay rates, branching fractions, and lepton-flavor ratios. The internal Lorentz prefactors use the same free quark--antiquark kinematics as the on-shell constituent spinors in the weak-current kernels, while the physical meson masses determine the external kinematics. For each model and decay channel, the two independent extractions of $f_-(q^2)$ using the $(+,\perp)$ and $(+,-)$ current-component combinations agree within numerical accuracy. We perform a direct analytic continuation of the spacelike overlap integrals in the $q^+=0$ frame using a mass-weighted contour in complex transverse momentum space. This yields the form factors throughout the physical timelike region, including zero recoil, without parametrizing their $q^2$ dependence. Form factors and differential decay rates are presented as equal-weight model averages with pointwise minimum--maximum bands. The light-lepton-averaged ratios range from $0.282$ to $0.301$ for $R(D)$ and from $0.287$ to $0.303$ for $R(D_s)$.
papers.reason: Global analysis of semileptonic B decays using light-front quark models and form factors provides useful hadronic matrix element methodology relevant to electroweak transitions.

papers.title: Spin Asymmetries for Twisted-Neutron Capture by Polarized $^3$He Nuclei
papers.abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of a nuclear reaction caused by twisted neutrons that carry an additional Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) along the propagation direction. Angular momentum selection rules are derived for the thermal-neutron capture reaction on a spin-polarized $^3$He nucleus. We demonstrate that noticeable novel spin effects due to OAM are limited to the region of the size of de Broglie wavelength around the phase singularity of the beam. Spin asymmetries are predicted for a range of experimental constraints.
papers.reason: Theoretical analysis of thermal-neutron capture by polarized 3He using twisted neutrons with orbital angular momentum, highly relevant to low-energy nuclear capture and spin asymmetries.

papers.title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
papers.abstract: This work investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson interferometry within the nonminimal Standard-Model Extension. Employing methods of chiral perturbation theory for mass dimension d=5, a connection between the quark-level and the meson effective pseudoscalar Lagrangian is established. The resulting phenomenological signatures in neutral-meson oscillations with particular focus on the detector geometry are explored. This analysis permits the interpretation of such CPT tests within the d=5 quark sector of the Standard-Model Extension. Existing data are used to extract first constraints on two coefficients and to estimate achievable sensitivity gains over published bounds of up to 18 orders of magnitude.
papers.reason: Investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson systems using chiral perturbation theory and the Standard-Model Extension, aligning with precision low-energy EFT tests.

papers.title: Next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to radiative decays of fully heavy tetraquarks into quarkonia
papers.abstract: Within nonrelativistic QCD factorization, we calculate the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the decays of compact $T_{4Q}=QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ states ($Q=c,b$) into an $S$-wave quarkonium and a photon. Conservation of charge conjugation allows $T_{4Q}^{0^{++}}$ and $T_{4Q}^{2^{++}}$ to decay into $V_Q+\gamma$, with $V_c=J/\psi$ and $V_b=\Upsilon$, while $T_{4Q}^{1^{+-}}$ can decay into $\eta_Q+\gamma$. At leading order in the heavy quark velocity expansion, we derive the short-distance coefficients for these decay widths in analytic form through $\mathcal{O}(\alpha\alpha_s^5)$, including the interference contribution between the two color configurations of $T_{4Q}^{0^{++}}$. All ultraviolet divergences at NLO are exactly canceled by renormalization. The NLO QCD corrections enhance the decay widths for $T_{4Q}^{2^{++}}\to V_Q+\gamma$ and $T_{4Q}^{1^{+-}}\to\eta_Q+\gamma$ by factors of approximately $2.94$ ($2.33$) and $2.22$ ($1.83$), respectively. The dependence on the renormalization scale $\mu_R$ is reduced at NLO in most channels, although it remains sizable. Based on the NLO branching fractions, we estimate yields of order $10^6$--$10^7$ for $T_{4c}\to J/\psi+\gamma$ and $10^4$ for $T_{4c}\to\eta_c+\gamma$ in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13~\mathrm{TeV}$ with an integrated luminosity of $100~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The $J/\psi+\gamma$ channels can be investigated through $J/\psi\to\ell^+\ell^-$ in the $\ell^+\ell^-\gamma$ invariant-mass spectrum, complementing di-charmonium searches.
papers.topic: NLO QCD for Heavy Tetraquark Decays
papers.reason: Calculates NLO QCD corrections to radiative decays of fully heavy tetraquarks into quarkonia within NRQCD factorization.

papers.title: Hadronic final-state effects on open-charm production at LHC energies
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of hadronic final-state interactions on open-charm observables in pp and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC energies within the microscopic Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) transport approach. Calculations with and without charm-hadron rescattering are compared with ALICE measurements and predictions of the Statistical Hadronization Model for charm. The relative integrated $D$-meson multiplicities are essentially insensitive to hadronic interactions. PHSD reproduces the weak system dependence of the nonstrange $D$-meson ratios and the increase of $D_s^+/D^0$ from pp to Pb+Pb collisions, consistent with the statistical-model trend from strangeness undersaturation towards equilibrium. In contrast, hadronic rescattering redistributes the transverse momentum spectra at low and intermediate momenta and enhances the elliptic flow. These results demonstrate the importance of accounting for the hadronic evolution when extracting QGP properties from differential open-charm observables.
papers.topic: Hadronic Final-State Effects on Open Charm
papers.reason: Investigates hadronic final-state interactions on open-charm observables using transport approaches, relevant to background and final-state interaction modeling akin to neutrino event generators.

papers.title: Role of Wigner SU(4) Symmetry in Low-Energy Spin-Isospin Transitions of Three-Valence-Nucleon Systems on LS Closed Cores
papers.abstract: We investigate low-energy Fermi (F) and Gamow--Teller (GT) transition strengths in three-valence-nucleon systems from the viewpoint of Wigner SU(4) symmetry. For $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$, shell-model calculations show that the ground states contain a large component of the SU(4) representation whose spin-isospin wave function is fully antisymmetric. By varying the spin--orbit splitting in the shell-model Hamiltonian, we demonstrate clear correlations of the SU(4) overlap with both the GT strength to the ground state and its fraction of the total GT strength. For $^{7}{\rm Li}$--$^{7}{\rm Be}$, shell-model calculations show that the $3/2^-_\mathrm{g.s.}$ and $1/2^-_1$ states both belong predominantly to the same supermultiplet as the $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground states. The observed strong GT transitions to these states are therefore interpreted as transitions within the same SU(4) multiplet, split by the spin-orbit interaction. Thus, Wigner SU(4) symmetry provides a unified interpretation of low-energy GT strength concentrations in three-valence-nucleon systems. In particular, the concentration of both F and GT strengths in the same $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground-state transition is naturally understood as a three-valence-nucleon extension of the SU(4) mechanism underlying the low-energy strong GT peak in $^{18}{\rm O}$--$^{18}{\rm F}$.
papers.reason: Examines Fermi and Gamow-Teller transition strengths in three-valence-nucleon systems through Wigner SU(4) symmetry, highly relevant to nuclear matrix elements for beta/neutrino transitions.

papers.title: SuperWIMPs in the Kination Era: Imprints on $N_{\rm eff}$ and CMB Spectral Distortions
papers.abstract: We investigate how the late-time decays of unstable particles into dark matter and neutrinos can leave measurable imprints on both cosmological observables and collider experiments. We study this mechanism within the scotogenic model, where the lightest singlet fermion $N_1$ serves as the dark matter candidate and is produced via the late decay of the lightest inert doublet scalar via the superWIMP mechanism. By incorporating a kination-dominated era in the early Universe, the altered expansion rate allows to match the observed $N_1$ relic density in parameter regions that would be underabundant in standard cosmology. The energy exchange between the injected neutrinos and photons resulting from the late-time decay can produce CMB spectral $\mu$-distortions, detectable shifts in the effective number of relativistic species $N_{\rm eff}$, or both simultaneously. Concentrating on the lightest component of inert doublet scalars with masses between $200$ and $500~\text{GeV}$, we find that these cosmological signals are accompanied by complementary signatures accessible at the LHC. Although our analysis is derived within the scotogenic framework, our findings apply more broadly to scenarios in which the unstable particle undergoes late-time out-of-equilibrium decay to produce dark matter and non-thermal neutrinos, offering how future CMB measurements and collider searches can jointly probe dark matter production and the early Universe's thermal history.
papers.reason: Studies late-time decays into dark matter and neutrinos producing CMB spectral distortions and Neff shifts within the scotogenic model, linking early universe neutrinos and BSM cosmology.

papers.title: Magnetic moments of the $\Sigma_c$ and $\Sigma_b$ baryons from external-field QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: We compute the magnetic moments of the $\Sigma_c$ and $\Sigma_b$ isotriplets with external-field QCD sum rules. The heavy-quark propagator is kept with its full mass dependence and with its couplings to the photon, to soft gluons and to both simultaneously, and the magnetic sum rule is normalized by the mass sum rule of the same interpolating field, which removes the residue and gives the baryon masses within a few percent. The quark-condensate magnetic susceptibility $\chi$, which otherwise dominates the uncertainty, is fixed by the proton magnetic moment computed with the same interpolating field; the neutron moment then follows to about $5\%$. Uncertainties from the QCD inputs are evaluated with a Monte Carlo analysis, and those from the interpolating field, the Borel window, the scale of the heavy-quark mass, the calibration and the normalization are added. With $\overline{\rm MS}$ heavy-quark masses we obtain $\mu_{\Sigma_c^{++}}=2.37\pm0.65$, $\mu_{\Sigma_c^{+}}=0.50\pm0.15$, $\mu_{\Sigma_c^{0}}=-1.39\pm0.37$, $\mu_{\Sigma_b^{+}}=2.16\pm0.65$, $\mu_{\Sigma_b^{0}}=0.55\pm0.16$ and $\mu_{\Sigma_b^{-}}=-1.06\pm0.32$ in nuclear magnetons; at this order the results depend sizably on the heavy-quark mass scheme. The moments are carried by the light diquark; the heavy-quark contribution, whose separation depends on the interpolating field, is $-0.13\pm0.02\,\mu_N$ for $\Sigma_c$ and $+0.013\pm0.003\,\mu_N$ for $\Sigma_b$.
papers.reason: Computes magnetic moments of Sigma_c and Sigma_b isotriplets using external-field QCD sum rules with heavy-quark mass dependence, relevant to heavy-baryon electromagnetic properties.

papers.title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
papers.abstract: The method of projection onto localized states intended for describing reactions and clustering is examined. In particular, the method offers a simple extension of the no-core shell model to continuum- and clusterized bound states. A critical analysis of a previous realization of the method is provided. A way to minimize the number of basis functions required for convergence is given. An easy way to obtain exactly unitary and symmetric $S$ matrix from calculations is pointed out. The method is tested in one- and two-channel $np$ scattering problems with the Daejeon $NN$ interaction. It is shown that excellent convergence can be reached even when only oscillator states with low number of excitation quanta are retained.
papers.topic: Projection onto localized states in reactions
papers.reason: Examines the method of projection onto localized states for describing reactions, clustering, and continuum extensions of the no-core shell model, highly relevant to ab initio nuclear reaction theory.

papers.title: Test beam results for machine-learning-based reconstruction of resistive silicon sensors
